central_claim_as_understood: Pooling the published EWSR1::NR4A3 vs TAF15::NR4A3 evidence across four literatures shows the fusion partner is a candidate, crude, and confounded prognostic stratifier — not yet an established or independent one — and round 8 correctly moved the 31-row correction appendix plus 15 inline notes and the falsifier's threshold derivation into disciplined, machine-checked form without dropping any content, including the one concession that nearly went missing.

p1s.where: §6, falsifier #5 ("Reconciling the two would take 19 further TAF15 patients with zero deaths — a total TAF15 denominator of 34, more than twice the pooled experience assembled here"); mirrored in emc-fusion-partner-pooling.json -> what_could_kill_this[4]
p1s.what: Round 8's whole point for R7-B4 was to DERIVE the falsifier threshold with zero_death_patients_to_reconcile() instead of asserting it, and this was re-run and independently reproduces 19/34/31.8%/30.4%/20.8% exactly from the committed COHORTS counts, so the numbers are correct today. But test_fusion_partner_prose_matches_its_artifact.py (the quantity guard) and mutate_fusion_partner_guard.py (the mutation harness) only bind/mutate the two projected percentages (31.8%/30.4%) and the comparator's 20.8% upper bound — grepped both files for '19 further', 'denominator of 34', 'total_taf15_denominator_required', 'further_zero_death_taf15_patients_required' and 'twice' and found zero matches. The '19', the '34' and the 'more than twice' relation — which are the actual headline output of the function round 8 built specifically so this class of number would never be typed by hand again — have no binding and no mutation, so a future correction to the TAF15 death arm's denominator/events or the comparator's counts could silently desync these three figures from the prose while every existing test stays green.
p1s.class_of_surface_unwatched: a derived quantity with a sibling quantity in the same sentence that IS bound — the guard covers the percentages next to it but not the integer counts, the exact one-of-a-pair shape (A19/A20, A24, A31) this paper's own correction history repeatedly names as its recurring failure mode
